pr.title: Add comprehensive email validation for blocked users

raw_findings.body: Users see a generic 'invalid' message for emails that were actually rejected because they are already registered, blacklisted, or blocked, obscuring the real reason and creating confusing UX (e.g., an already-registered user cannot tell they should log in instead).
raw_findings.failure_mode: Loss of diagnostic information shown to the end user, degrading UX for legitimate failure causes.
raw_findings.impact: Users see a generic 'invalid' message for emails that were actually rejected because they are already registered, blacklisted, or blocked, obscuring the real reason and creating confusing UX (e.g., an already-registered user cannot tell they should log in instead).
raw_findings.root_cause: The new rejectedEmails check discards the actual server error text and substitutes a single generic message.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Preserve and surface the specific server-provided error message/reason instead of hardcoding I18n.t('user.email.invalid').
raw_findings.title: Rejected-email reason always shown as generic 'invalid' regardless of actual server-side failure reason
raw_findings.trigger: Server rejects an email for any reason (blocked, blacklisted domain, or already taken) and the client re-renders emailValidation for that same value.

raw_findings.body: The exact-match lookup fails to find the blocked record, so should_block? returns false and the blocking mechanism is silently bypassed, defeating the feature's purpose.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Security/feature bypass — blocked users can register by changing letter case in their email.
raw_findings.impact: The exact-match lookup fails to find the blocked record, so should_block? returns false and the blocking mechanism is silently bypassed, defeating the feature's purpose.
raw_findings.root_cause: New lookup does not normalize email case before querying, unlike the pre-existing blacklist/whitelist regex checks which explicitly used case-insensitive matching.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Normalize case (e.g. downcase both the stored email and lookup value, or add a case-insensitive index/query) before comparing.
raw_findings.title: Case-sensitive lookup in BlockedEmail.should_block? allows bypass by varying email case
raw_findings.trigger: A blocked email is stored as 'user@spam.com' and a signup attempt is made with 'User@Spam.com' (different case) on a case-sensitive collation database (default Postgres).

raw_findings.body: Both requests load the same match_count value, increment it independently, and save, so one increment is lost — match_count under-reports the true number of matches.
raw_findings.evidence:
def self.should_block?(email)
    record = BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first
    if record
      record.match_count += 1
      record.last_match_at = Time.zone.now
      record.save
    end
    record && record.action_type == actions[:block]
  end
raw_findings.failure_mode: Race condition causes silently incorrect analytics/counters.
raw_findings.impact: Both requests load the same match_count value, increment it independently, and save, so one increment is lost — match_count under-reports the true number of matches.
raw_findings.root_cause: Statistics update uses in-memory read-then-write instead of an atomic database operation.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use an atomic update such as `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).update_all(['match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ?', Time.zone.now])` or wrap in a DB-level increment/transaction with locking.
raw_findings.title: Non-atomic read-modify-write in BlockedEmail.should_block? causes lost updates under concurrent signups
raw_findings.trigger: Two concurrent signup requests use the same blocked email simultaneously.

raw_findings.body: BlockedEmail.should_block? mutates and persists match_count/last_match_at as a side effect of a validation call; because validations run at least twice per signup attempt, match_count is incremented more than once per actual attempt, corrupting the blocking statistics.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Data integrity — recorded match statistics no longer correspond to actual distinct signup attempts.
raw_findings.impact: BlockedEmail.should_block? mutates and persists match_count/last_match_at as a side effect of a validation call; because validations run at least twice per signup attempt, match_count is incremented more than once per actual attempt, corrupting the blocking statistics.
raw_findings.root_cause: A validator now performs persistent side effects, which conflicts with Rails calling validations multiple times (valid? and save) within a single logical request.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Move the side-effecting counter update out of the validator (e.g., only record a match after the user record is actually persisted/rejected), or memoize should_block? per validation run.
raw_findings.title: Side-effecting validator can run multiple times per request, inflating BlockedEmail match statistics
raw_findings.trigger: UsersController#create calls `user.valid?` (unconditionally, since `if user.valid? && SiteSetting.call_discourse_hub?` evaluates valid? first) and later calls `user.save`, which re-runs all validations including this one, for the same signup attempt.

raw_findings.body: Inconsistent with the rest of the codebase (which uses `&&`), making the code harder to maintain and increasing risk if the expression is later extended with assignment, where `and`'s low precedence differs from `&&`.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Maintainability/style inconsistency; latent precedence footgun for future edits.
raw_findings.impact: Inconsistent with the rest of the codebase (which uses `&&`), making the code harder to maintain and increasing risk if the expression is later extended with assignment, where `and`'s low precedence differs from `&&`.
raw_findings.root_cause: New code introduces the `and` keyword instead of following the project's established `&&` convention.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Replace `and` with `&&` to match existing style used elsewhere (e.g., blocked_email.rb, create_account_controller.js).
raw_findings.title: Use of low-precedence 'and' instead of '&&' in conditional deviates from codebase convention
raw_findings.trigger: Code review / static analysis of new validator file; any future edit that appends an assignment to this line could hit `and`'s low-precedence pitfall.

raw_findings.body: The new client-side logic that records rejected emails and re-validates emailValidation against them has no automated test, so regressions (e.g., the shared-array bug) would not be caught by CI.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Reduced review/regression-detection quality for newly introduced client logic.
raw_findings.impact: The new client-side logic that records rejected emails and re-validates emailValidation against them has no automated test, so regressions (e.g., the shared-array bug) would not be caught by CI.
raw_findings.root_cause: New client behavior was added without corresponding unit tests.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add a QUnit/Ember test that simulates a failed createAccount response with result.errors.email and result.values.email, and asserts rejectedEmails/emailValidation update correctly and are scoped per controller instance.
raw_findings.title: No test coverage for new rejectedEmails client-side tracking behavior
raw_findings.trigger: A signup request fails with an email-related server error.
